feed.title: [BIP Draft] Segregated Data: a prunable, script-isolated block region for data carriage

entry.title: [BIP Draft] Segregated Data: a prunable, script-isolated block region for data carriage
entry.summary:
The discussion revolves around the intricacies of SegData entries and block weight in regard to consensus relevance. It is established that while SegData entries themselves do not affect consensus, the weight of a block does play a crucial role in the validation process. This leads to the acknowledgment that constructing a block smaller than what is permitted remains a valid approach within the system.
Further exploration into the proposal reveals that it inherently supports SegData being enabled by default. The counterargument which advocates for disabling SegData by default represents a separate proposition altogether. The rationale behind recommending the deactivation of SegData in most node setup guides is primarily to reduce the data footprint, emphasizing efficiency and manageability in node operations.
Moreover, there appears to be a lack of incentive for maintaining SegData as an active feature by default, suggesting a general consensus or expectation that its impact or utility may not justify the potential increase in data requirements. This sentiment is reiterated to emphasize its perceived minimal influence or interest in the broader scheme of blockchain management and operation strategies.
